indicator_definition: This indicator measures the proportion of surface water bodies (rivers, lakes, transitional and coastal waters) achieving good or high ecological status or potential, as defined by the EU Water Framework Directive. It is expressed as a percentage of all assessed water bodies. Data are reported by member states every six years.
rationale: The ecological status of water bodies reflects the overall health of aquatic ecosystems and the pressures they face from human activities. Achieving good ecological status is the central objective of the Water Framework Directive. Progress means an increasing proportion of surface water bodies achieving good or high ecological status.
methodology_characteristics: Data are reported by EU member states to the European Environment Agency (EEA) under the Water Framework Directive (2000/60/EC). Ecological status is assessed based on biological, hydromorphological and physico-chemical quality elements. Reporting cycles run every six years.
indicator_name: Water bodies with good ecological status
